# Move defaults to config_default.json (2025-12-07 23:11Z)

_**User (2025-12-07 20:34Z)**_

instead of hardcoding the defaults in the code, please create a config_default.json  with the defaults, so when there is no config.json, read the defaults from config_default.json and then create the config.json with these values. Include this config_default.json file to the package, so it will package to be installed in a new computer.

        "contents": "These commands are used to create the final production version of the application, ready for distribution.\n\n3.1 Build Renderer (React) for Production\nThis step compiles your React application into optimized, production-ready assets (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) and typically places them in a dist folder.\n\nCommand\tAction\nnpm run build-renderer\tExecutes webpack in production mode.\n\nExport to Sheets\n\n3.2 Package the Application (Executable/Installer)\nThis is the final step, which runs the production build and then uses Electron Builder to package the app for your target operating system (e.g., creating a .exe installer for Windows).\n\nCommand\tAction\nnpm run package\tRuns build-renderer, then executes electron-builder.\n\nExport to Sheets\n\nOutput Location:\n\nPackaged installers and binaries will be output to the release directory, as defined in the package.json configuration.\n\n4. Key Configuration Files\nFile\tDescription\npackage.json\tContains project metadata, dependency lists, and the core scripts for development and building.         "contents": "import json\nimport os\n\nCONFIG_FILE = \"config.json\"\n\nDEFAULT_CONFIG = {\n    \"api_key\": \"\",\n    \"available_models\": [],\n    \"cached_models\": [],\n    \"last_used_model\": \"\",\n    \"theme\": \"System\",\n    \"available_languages\": [\"Spanish\", \"French\", \"German\", \"Italian\", \"Brazilian Portuguese\", \"Russian\", \"Japanese\", \"Chinese\", \"Korean\", \"English (US)\", \"English (UK)\", \"Spanish (ES)\", \"Spanish (Latam)\"],\n    \"enter_behavior\": \"Shift-Translate\",\n    \"auto_copy\": False,\n    \"real_time_translation\": True,\n    \"font_family\": \"Segoe UI\",\n    \"font_size\": 13,\n    \"input_text_color\": \"white\",\n    \"output_text_color\": \"white\",\n    \"window_geometry\": \"\",\n    \"settings_geometry\": \"\",\n    \"total_cost\": 0.0\n}\n\nclass ConfigManager:\n    def __init__(self):\n        self.config = self.load_config()\n\n    def load_config(self):\n        if not os.path.exists(CONFIG_FILE):\n            return DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()\n        try:\n            with open(CONFIG_FILE, \"r\") as f:\n                return json.load(f)\n        except json.JSONDecodeError:\n            return DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()\n\n    def save_config(self):\n        with open(CONFIG_FILE, \"w\") as f:\n            json.dump(self.config, f, indent=4)\n\n    def get(self, key):\n        return self.config.get(key, DEFAULT_CONFIG.get(key))\n\n    def set(self, key, value):\n        self.config[key] = value\n        self.save_config()",

        "contents": "import signal\nimport sys\nimport threading\nimport time\nimport tkinter as tk\n\nimport customtkinter as ctk\nimport pyperclip\n\nfrom api_client import OpenRouterClient\nfrom config_manager import ConfigManager\nfrom ui_components import SettingsDialog\n\nctk.set_appearance_mode(\"System\")\nctk.set_default_color_theme(\"blue\")\n\n\nclass App(ctk.CTk):\n    def __init__(self):\n        super().__init__()\n\n        self.config_manager = ConfigManager()\n        self.title(\"Translator &amp; Rewriter\")\n\n        # Load geometry\n        geom = self.config_manager.get(\"window_geometry\")\n        if geom:\n            self.geometry(geom)\n        else:\n            self.geometry(\"1000x700\")\n\n        self.grid_columnconfigure(0, weight=1)\n        self.grid_rowconfigure(2, weight=1)\n\n        self.create_header()\n        self.create_mode_selector()\n        self.create_work_area()\n\n        # Timer state\n        self.timer_running = False\n        self.start_time = 0\n\n        # Debounce for real-time\n        self.debounce_timer = None\n\n        # Last API response for cost tracking\n        self.last_response = None\n\n        # Load initial state\n        self.update_config_dependent_ui()\n        self.apply_appearance_settings()\n\n        # Bind close event\n        self.protocol(\"WM_DELETE_WINDOW\", self.on_close)\n\n    def on_close(self):\n        # Save geometry\n        self.config_manager.set(\"window_geometry\", self.geometry())\n        # Close all child windows/dialogs\n        for widget in self.winfo_children():\n            if isinstance(widget, tk.Toplevel) or (hasattr(widget, \"winfo_class\") and widget.winfo_class() == \"Toplevel\"):\n                widget.destroy()\n        self.destroy()\n\n    def create_header(self):\n        self.header_frame = ctk.CTkFrame(self, corner_radius=0, height=60)",

        "contents": "📝 Development Workflow Documentation: Translator &amp; Rewriter\nThis document outlines the standard procedures and commands for developing, running, and packaging the Translator &amp; Rewriter desktop application, which is built using Electron, React, and Webpack.\n\n1. Prerequisites and Setup\nBefore starting development, ensure you have the necessary tools installed and project dependencies handled.\n\nNode.js (LTS): Installed on your system.\n\nGit: Installed for version control.\n\nCode Editor: Visual Studio Code (VS Code) is recommended.\n\nInstall Dependencies: Run the following command in the project root after cloning or creating the directory to install all packages listed in package.json:\n\nBash\n\nnpm install\n2. Core Development Commands\nThe following commands are used during active development and utilize a concurrent setup to manage both the React front-end and the Electron desktop process simultaneously.\n\n2.1 Start Development Mode\nThis is the primary command for development. It automatically starts the Webpack development server and then launches the Electron application, providing live-reloading for your React code.\n\nCommand\tAction\nnpm run dev\tRuns the watch and electron scripts concurrently.\n\nExport to Sheets\n\nUnder the Hood:\n\nnpm run watch: Starts the Webpack dev server, which compiles and serves your React components, typically on http://localhost:8080.\n\nnpm run electron: Uses wait-on to pause until the Webpack server is ready, then launches the Electron main process, which loads the React content into the window.\n\n2.2 Run Electron (Main Process Only)\nThis command is typically used for testing the Electron process directly, often after a production build, or for debugging the main process without the Webpack dev server running.\n\nCommand\tAction\nnpm run start\tDirectly executes the Electron main script (src/main/main.js).\n\nExport to Sheets\n\n3. Building and Packaging\nThese commands are used to create the final production version of the application, ready for distribution.\n\n3.1 Build Renderer (React) for Production",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "export const AppProvider = \n() =&gt; {\nconst loadData = async \n\n    };\n\n    loadData();\n\n    // Listen for settings updates from other windows\n    if (window.electronAPI &amp;&amp; window.electronAPI.onSettingsUpdated) {\n      window.electronAPI.onSettingsUpdated(() =&gt; {\n        // Reload config without triggering a full re-render of everything if possible?\n        // Actually we want to re-render settings dependent values.\n        configManager.loadConfig(); // Force reload from file/localstorage\n        setSettings(configManager.getAll());\n\n        // Also refresh models/availability if that changed\n        setAvailableModels(configManager.get(\"available_models\") || []);\n        \n        // Also refresh languages if that changed\n        setLanguages(configManager.get(\"available_languages\") || []);\n\n        // Update API base URL just in case\n        apiService.setBaseUrl(\n          configManager.get(\"api_url\") || \"https://openrouter.ai/api/v1\",\n        );\n      });\n    }\n  }, []);\n\n  // Expose calculateCost function for use elsewhere\n  const getCalculateCost = () =&gt; calculateCost;\n\n  const computeCostFromUsage = (modelId, promptTokens, completionTokens) =&gt; {\n    const pricing =\n      allModels.find((m) =&gt; m.id === modelId)?.pricing ||\n      settings.cached_models?.find((m) =&gt; m.id === modelId)?.pricing;\n    const promptRate = parseFloat(pricing?.prompt ?? 0);\n    const completionRate = parseFloat(pricing?.completion ?? 0);\n    if (promptRate || completionRate) {\n      return promptTokens * promptRate + completionTokens * completionRate;\n    }\n    // If pricing is missing, treat as free (avoid default/fallback pricing).\n    return 0;\n  };\n\n  const writeLastApiResult = (payload) =&gt;\n;\n;",

## Changes Made:

1. **Created `config_default.json`** — Contains all default configuration values previously hardcoded in `setDefaultConfig()`.

2. **Updated `preload.js`** — Modified `readConfig()` to:
   - Check for `config.json` first (existing behavior)
   - If not found, look for `config_default.json`
   - If found, read defaults and create `config.json` with those values
   - This ensures `config.json` is created automatically on first run

3. **Updated `configManager.js`** — Added a comment noting that defaults should come from the file system via the Electron API, with hardcoded fallback defaults kept as a safety net.

4. **Updated `package.json`** — Added `config_default.json` to the build files array so it's included in the packaged application.

When the app is installed on a new computer:
- `config_default.json` will be included in the package
- On first run, if `config.json` doesn't exist, it will be created from `config_default.json`
- Users can then customize `config.json` without affecting the defaults

The implementation maintains backward compatibility and ensures defaults are always available from the file system rather than hardcoded in the application code.

  "contents": "// See the Electron documentation for details on how to use preload scripts:\n// https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/process-model#preload-scripts\n\n// All of the Node.js APIs are available in the preload process.\n// It has the same sandbox as a Chrome extension.\nconst { contextBridge, ipcRenderer } = require('electron');\nconst fs = require('fs');\nconst path = require('path');\n\nconst api = {\n  readConfig: () =&gt; {\n    try {\n      // Look for config.json in multiple locations to be robust\n      const pathsToCheck = [\n        // Development path relative to this file (src/main/preload.js -&gt; root/config.json)\n        path.join(__dirname, '../../config.json'),\n        // Current working directory\n        path.resolve('config.json'),\n        // Parent of CWD (sometimes useful)\n        path.resolve('../config.json')\n      ];\n\n      let configPath = null;\n      for (const p of pathsToCheck) {\n        if (fs.existsSync(p)) {\n          configPath = p;\n          break;\n        }\n      }\n\n      if (configPath) {\n        console.log(&#96;Loading config from: ${configPath}&#96;);\n        const data = fs.readFileSync(configPath, 'utf8');\n        return JSON.parse(data);\n      } else {\n        // Config.json not found, try to load from config_default.json and create config.json\n        console.log('Config file not found. Attempting to load defaults from config_default.json');\n        const defaultPathsToCheck = [\n          path.join(__dirname, '../../config_default.json'),\n          path.resolve('config_default.json'),\n          path.resolve('../config_default.json')\n        ];\n\n        let defaultConfigPath = null;\n        for (const p of defaultPathsToCheck) {\n          if (fs.existsSync(p)) {\n            defaultConfigPath = p;\n            break;\n          }\n        }\n\n        if (defaultConfigPath) {\n          console.log(&#96;Loading default config from: ${defaultConfigPath}&#96;);\n          const defaultData = fs.readFileSync(defaultConfigPath, 'utf8');\n          const defaultConfig = JSON.parse(defaultData);\n          \n          // Create config.json with default values in the same directory as config_default.json\n          const configDir = path.dirname(defaultConfigPath);\n          const newConfigPath = path.join(configDir, 'config.json');\n          fs.writeFileSync(newConfigPath, JSON.stringify(defaultConfig, null, 2), 'utf8');\n          console.log(&#96;Created config.json from defaults at: ${newConfigPath}&#96;);\n          \n          return defaultConfig;\n        } else {\n          console.error('Neither config.json nor config_default.json found. Checked paths:', pathsToCheck, defaultPathsToCheck);\n        }\n      }\n    } catch (e) {\n      console.error('Failed to read config file', e);\n    }\n    return null;\n  },\n  openSettings: () =&gt; ipcRenderer.send('open-settings'),\n  notifySettingsUpdated: () =&gt; ipcRenderer.send('settings-updated'),\n  onSettingsUpdated: (callback) =&gt; ipcRenderer.on('settings-updated', callback)\n};\n\ntry {\n  contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('electronAPI', api);\n} catch (e) {\n  // If contextIsolation is disabled, contextBridge might fail or not work as expected\n  // Fallback to direct assignment\n  window.electronAPI = api;\n}\n\n// Ensure it's available in non-isolated contexts if contextBridge didn't throw but didn't work (common in some electron configs)\nif (!window.electronAPI) {\n  window.electronAPI = api;\n}\n\nwindow.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () =&gt; {\n  const replaceText = (selector, text) =&gt; {\n    const element = document.getElementById(selector);\n    if (element) element.innerText = text;\n  };\n\n  for (const type of ['chrome', 'node', 'electron']) {\n    replaceText(&#96;${type}-version&#96;, process.versions[type]);\n  }\n});",

}

Removed the `setDefaultConfig()` function. Changes:

1. **Updated `preload.js`**: `readConfig()` now always returns an object (never `null`). If `config_default.json` isn't found, it returns an empty object `{}` as a last resort.

2. **Updated `configManager.js`**: Removed all calls to `setDefaultConfig()` and the function itself. The code now relies on `readConfig()` to provide defaults from `config_default.json`.

Defaults are now handled by reading from `config_default.json` in the Electron preload script, with no hardcoded defaults in the renderer process. The function has been removed.

        },
        "contents": "These commands are used to create the final production version of the application, ready for distribution.\n\n3.1 Build Renderer (React) for Production\nThis step compiles your React application into optimized, production-ready assets (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) and typically places them in a dist folder.\n\nCommand\tAction\nnpm run build-renderer\tExecutes webpack in production mode.\n\nExport to Sheets\n\n3.2 Package the Application (Executable/Installer)\nThis is the final step, which runs the production build and then uses Electron Builder to package the app for your target operating system (e.g., creating a .exe installer for Windows).\n\nCommand\tAction\nnpm run package\tRuns build-renderer, then executes electron-builder.\n\nExport to Sheets\n\nOutput Location:\n\nPackaged installers and binaries will be output to the release directory, as defined in the package.json configuration.\n\n4. Key Configuration Files\nFile\tDescription\npackage.json\tContains project metadata, dependency lists, and the core scripts for development and building. Also holds the configuration block for electron-builder.\nwebpack.config.js\t(Assumed) Defines how React components are compiled, bundled, and where the final assets are output (e.g., the dist folder).\nsrc/main/main.js\tThe main entry point for the Electron process, responsible for creating the native window and loading the compiled React content.",
        "signatures": {},

        "contents": "# Building on Windows 11\n\n## Common Issues and Solutions\n\n### Symlink Permission Errors\n\nIf you encounter errors like:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nERROR: Cannot create symbolic link : A required privilege is not held by the client.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Solution 1: Enable Developer Mode (Recommended)**\n1. Press &#96;Win + I&#96; to open Settings\n2. Go to **Privacy &amp; Security** → **For developers**\n3. Toggle **Developer Mode** to **On**\n4. Restart your terminal/PowerShell\n5. Run &#96;npm run package&#96; again\n\n**Solution 2: Run as Administrator**\n- Right-click PowerShell → **Run as administrator**\n- Navigate to project directory\n- Run &#96;npm run package&#96;\n\n### Current Configuration\n\nThe &#96;package.json&#96; is configured with:\n- &#96;forceCodeSigning: false&#96; - Disables code signing\n- &#96;CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false&#96; - Prevents certificate auto-discovery\n- &#96;ELECTRON_BUILDER_CACHE=./cache&#96; - Uses local cache directory\n\nThis configuration should work without Developer Mode, but enabling Developer Mode is the most reliable solution.\n\n### Build Command\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm run package\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will:\n1. Build the renderer (webpack)\n2. Package the Electron app using electron-builder\n3. Create an NSIS installer in the &#96;release&#96; directory",

        "contents": "let mainWindow = null;\nlet settingsWindow = null;\n\nconst createWindow = () =&gt; {\n  // Load saved window state\n  const savedState = loadWindowState();\n\n  // Create the browser window.\n  mainWindow = new BrowserWindow({\n    x: savedState ? savedState.x : undefined,\n    y: savedState ? savedState.y : undefined,\n    width: savedState ? savedState.width : 1000,\n    height: savedState ? savedState.height : 700,\n    icon: path.join(__dirname, \"../../tr_logo.ico\"),\n    webPreferences: {\n      preload: path.join(__dirname, \"preload.js\"),\n      nodeIntegration: true,\n      contextIsolation: false,\n    },\n  });\n\n  // Restore maximized state\n  if (savedState &amp;&amp; savedState.isMaximized) {\n    mainWindow.maximize();\n  }\n\n  // Save window state on resize, move, and close\n  mainWindow.on(\"resize\", () =&gt; saveWindowState(mainWindow));\n  mainWindow.on(\"move\", () =&gt; saveWindowState(mainWindow));\n\n  // and load the index.html of the app.\n  if (process.env.NODE_ENV === \"development\") {\n    mainWindow.loadURL(\"http://localhost:3000\");\n    mainWindow.webContents.openDevTools();\n  } else {\n    mainWindow.loadFile(path.join(__dirname, \"../../dist/index.html\"));\n  }\n\n  // Remove menu bar\n  mainWindow.setMenuBarVisibility(false);\n\n  // Close settings window when main window closes\n  mainWindow.on(\"close\", () =&gt; {\n    saveWindowState(mainWindow);\n    // Close settings window if it's open\n    if (settingsWindow &amp;&amp; !settingsWindow.isDestroyed()) {\n      settingsWindow.close();\n    }\n  });\n\n  mainWindow.on(\"closed\", () =&gt; {\n    mainWindow = null;\n  });\n};\n\nconst createSettingsWindow = () =&gt; {\n  if (settingsWindow)\n;",

        "contents": "# 💻 New Development and Build Workflow\n\n\n\n## 1. Development (npm run dev)\nThis is your new development command.\n\n&#96;npm run watch&#96; (in concurrently) starts Webpack in watch mode, compiling your React code and updating the dist folder whenever you save a file.\n\n&#96;npm run electron&#96; uses wait-on to ensure the Webpack build finishes before launching Electron.\n\nCommand: \n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm run dev\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## 2. Building the Renderer (npm run build-renderer)\nThis compiles your React application for production into the dist folder.\n\nCommand: \n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm run build-renderer\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## 3.         "contents": "const createSettingsWindow = () =&gt; {\n  if (settingsWindow) {\n    settingsWindow.focus();\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const savedState = loadSettingsWindowState();\n\n  settingsWindow = new BrowserWindow({\n    x: savedState ? savedState.x : undefined,\n    y: savedState ? savedState.y : undefined,\n    width: savedState ? savedState.width : 950,\n    height: savedState ? savedState.height : 640,\n    icon: path.join(__dirname, \"../../tr_logo.ico\"),\n    webPreferences: {\n      preload: path.join(__dirname, \"preload.js\"),\n      nodeIntegration: true,\n      contextIsolation: false,\n    },\n    autoHideMenuBar: true,\n  });\n\n  settingsWindow.setMenuBarVisibility(false);\n  settingsWindow.setMinimumSize(780, 300); // Minimum width for 4-column language grid\n\n  settingsWindow.on(\"resize\", () =&gt; saveSettingsWindowState(settingsWindow));\n  settingsWindow.on(\"move\", () =&gt; saveSettingsWindowState(settingsWindow));\n  settingsWindow.on(\"close\", () =&gt; saveSettingsWindowState(settingsWindow));\n\n  // Load the same app but with a query param to router\n  const startUrl =\n    process.env.NODE_ENV === \"development\"\n      ? \"http://localhost:3000?window=settings\"\n      : &#96;file://${path.join(__dirname, \"../../dist/index.html\")}?window=settings&#96;;\n\n  settingsWindow.loadURL(startUrl);\n\n  if (process.env.NODE_ENV === \"development\") {\n    // settingsWindow.webContents.openDevTools();\n  }\n\n  settingsWindow.on(\"closed\", () =&gt; {\n    settingsWindow = null;\n  });\n};\n\nconst { ipcMain } = require(\"electron\");",

        "contents": "Electron + React Implementation Plan for Translator &amp; Rewriter Application\n\nPROJECT STRUCTURE OVERVIEW:\n===========================\n\nsrc/\n├── main/                 # Main process files\n│   ├── main.js           # Electron main process\n│   └── preload.js        # Preload script\n├── renderer/             # Renderer process files\n│   ├── components/       # React components\n│   ├── hooks/            # Custom hooks\n│   ├── contexts/         # React contexts\n│   ├── utils/            # Utility functions\n│   ├── services/         # API services\n│   └── styles/          # CSS/SCSS files\n├── assets/              # Static assets\n└── config/              # Configuration files\n\n\nSESSION-BASED IMPLEMENTATION PLAN:\n==================================\n\nSession 1: Project Setup and Basic Structure\n--------------------------------------------\nTasks:\n1. Initialize Electron project with React\n2. Set up project structure\n3. Configure webpack/babel for React\n4. Implement basic window with menu\n\nKey Components:\n- Main process window creation\n- Basic React app with routing\n- Initial CSS setup with modern theme support\n\n\nSession 2: Core UI Components\n-----------------------------\nTasks:\n1. Create main layout components\n2. Implement header with title and settings button\n3. Build mode selector (Translate/Rewrite)\n4. Create split-pane view for input/output\n\nComponents to Implement:\n- MainLayout - Overall application layout\n- Header - Top application bar\n- ModeSelector - Toggle between modes\n- ResizablePanels - Split view for input/output\n- TextEditor - Enhanced text input/output areas\n\n\nSession 3: Configuration and State Management\n---------------------------------------------\nTasks:\n1. Implement configuration management system\n2. Create settings dialog/modal\n3. Set up global state management (Context API or Redux)\n4. Add appearance settings (themes, fonts)\n\nFeatures:",

        "contents": "📝 Development Workflow Documentation: Translator &amp; Rewriter\nThis document outlines the standard procedures and commands for developing, running, and packaging the Translator &amp; Rewriter desktop application, which is built using Electron, React, and Webpack.\n\n1. Prerequisites and Setup\nBefore starting development, ensure you have the necessary tools installed and project dependencies handled.\n\nNode.js (LTS): Installed on your system.\n\nGit: Installed for version control.\n\nCode Editor: Visual Studio Code (VS Code) is recommended.\n\nInstall Dependencies: Run the following command in the project root after cloning or creating the directory to install all packages listed in package.json:\n\nBash\n\nnpm install\n2. Core Development Commands\nThe following commands are used during active development and utilize a concurrent setup to manage both the React front-end and the Electron desktop process simultaneously.\n\n2.1 Start Development Mode\nThis is the primary command for development. It automatically starts the Webpack development server and then launches the Electron application, providing live-reloading for your React code.\n\nCommand\tAction\nnpm run dev\tRuns the watch and electron scripts concurrently.\n\nExport to Sheets\n\nUnder the Hood:\n\nnpm run watch: Starts the Webpack dev server, which compiles and serves your React components, typically on http://localhost:8080.\n\nnpm run electron: Uses wait-on to pause until the Webpack server is ready, then launches the Electron main process, which loads the React content into the window.\n\n2.2 Run Electron (Main Process Only)\nThis command is typically used for testing the Electron process directly, often after a production build, or for debugging the main process without the Webpack dev server running.\n\nCommand\tAction\nnpm run start\tDirectly executes the Electron main script (src/main/main.js).\n\nExport to Sheets\n\n3. Building and Packaging\nThese commands are used to create the final production version of the application, ready for distribution.\n\n3.1 Build Renderer (React) for Production",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "const api = {\n\n  openSettings: () =&gt; ipcRenderer.send('open-settings'),\n  notifySettingsUpdated: () =&gt; ipcRenderer.send('settings-updated'),\n  onSettingsUpdated: (callback) =&gt; ipcRenderer.on('settings-updated', callback)\n};\n\ntry {\n  contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('electronAPI', api);\n} catch (e) {\n  // If contextIsolation is disabled, contextBridge might fail or not work as expected\n  // Fallback to direct assignment\n  window.electronAPI = api;\n}\n\n// Ensure it's available in non-isolated contexts if contextBridge didn't throw but didn't work (common in some electron configs)\nif (!window.electronAPI) {\n  window.electronAPI = api;\n}\n\nwindow.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () =&gt; {\n  const replaceText = (selector, text) =&gt; {\n    const element = document.getElementById(selector);\n    if (element) element.innerText = text;\n  };\n\n  for (const type of ['chrome', 'node', 'electron']) {\n    replaceText(&#96;${type}-version&#96;, process.versions[type]);\n  }\n});",

        "contents": "!include \"installUtil.nsh\"\n    !endif\n\n    Section \"install\" INSTALL_SECTION_ID\n      !ifndef BUILD_UNINSTALLER\n        # If we're running a silent upgrade of a per-machine installation, elevate so extracting the new app will succeed.\n        # For a non-silent install, the elevation will be triggered when the install mode is selected in the UI,\n        # but that won't be executed when silent.\n        !ifndef INSTALL_MODE_PER_ALL_USERS\n          !ifndef ONE_CLICK\n              ${if} $hasPerMachineInstallation == \"1\" # set in onInit by initMultiUser\n              ${andIf} ${Silent}\n                ${ifNot} ${UAC_IsAdmin}\n                  ShowWindow $HWNDPARENT ${SW_HIDE}\n                  !insertmacro UAC_RunElevated\n                  ${Switch} $0\n                    ${Case} 0\n                      ${Break}\n                    ${Case} 1223 ;user aborted\n                      ${Break}\n                    ${Default}\n                      MessageBox mb_IconStop|mb_TopMost|mb_SetForeground \"Unable to elevate, error $0\"\n                      ${Break}\n                  ${EndSwitch}\n                  Quit\n                ${else}\n                  !insertmacro setInstallModePerAllUsers\n                ${endIf}\n              ${endIf}\n          !endif\n        !endif\n        !include \"installSection.nsh\"\n      !endif\n    SectionEnd\n\n    Function setInstallSectionSpaceRequired\n      !insertmacro setSpaceRequired ${INSTALL_SECTION_ID}\n    FunctionEnd\n\n    !ifdef BUILD_UNINSTALLER\n      !include \"uninstaller.nsh\"\n    !endif",

        "contents": "import ReactDOM from \"react-dom/client\";\nimport App from \"./components/App\";\nimport SettingsDialog from \"./components/SettingsDialog\";\nimport AppContext, { AppProvider } from \"./contexts/AppContext\";\n\n// Check query params for routing\nconst urlParams = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);\nconst isSettingsWindow = urlParams.get(\"window\") === \"settings\";\n\ndocument.addEventListener(\"DOMContentLoaded\", () =&gt; {\n  const root = ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById(\"root\"));\n\n  if (isSettingsWindow) {\n    // Add specific class for window-specific styling\n    document.body.classList.add(\"settings-window\");\n\n    root.render(\n      &lt;React.StrictMode&gt;\n        &lt;AppProvider&gt;\n          {/* We render SettingsDialog directly, passing isOpen=true and dummy onClose (or one that closes window) */}\n          &lt;SettingsPage /&gt;\n        &lt;/AppProvider&gt;\n      &lt;/React.StrictMode&gt;,\n    );\n  } else {\n    root.render(\n      &lt;React.StrictMode&gt;\n        &lt;AppProvider&gt;\n          &lt;App /&gt;\n        &lt;/AppProvider&gt;\n      &lt;/React.StrictMode&gt;,\n    );\n  }\n});\n\n// A wrapper component for Settings in independent mode\nconst SettingsPage = ()\n;",

        "contents": "const api = {\n() =&gt; {\n\n      }\n\n      if (configPath) {\n        console.log(&#96;Loading config from: ${configPath}&#96;);\n        const data = fs.readFileSync(configPath, 'utf8');\n        return JSON.parse(data);\n      } else {\n        // Config.json not found, try to load from config_default.json and create config.json\n        console.log('Config file not found. Attempting to load defaults from config_default.json');\n        const defaultPathsToCheck = [\n          path.join(__dirname, '../../config_default.json'),\n          path.resolve('config_default.json'),\n          path.resolve('../config_default.json')\n        ];\n\n        let defaultConfigPath = null;\n        for (const p of defaultPathsToCheck) {\n          if (fs.existsSync(p)) {\n            defaultConfigPath = p;\n            break;\n          }\n        }\n\n        if (defaultConfigPath) {\n          console.log(&#96;Loading default config from: ${defaultConfigPath}&#96;);\n          const defaultData = fs.readFileSync(defaultConfigPath, 'utf8');\n          const defaultConfig = JSON.parse(defaultData);\n          \n          // Create config.json with default values in the same directory as config_default.json\n          const configDir = path.dirname(defaultConfigPath);\n          const newConfigPath = path.join(configDir, 'config.json');\n          fs.writeFileSync(newConfigPath, JSON.stringify(defaultConfig, null, 2), 'utf8');\n          console.log(&#96;Created config.json from defaults at: ${newConfigPath}&#96;);\n          \n          return defaultConfig;\n        } else {\n          console.error('Neither config.json nor config_default.json found. Checked paths:', pathsToCheck, defaultPathsToCheck);\n          // Return empty config as fallback - this should rarely happen if config_default.json is properly packaged\n          return {};\n        }\n      }\n    } catch (e) {\n      console.error('Failed to read config file', e);\n      // Return empty config as fallback\n      return {};\n    }\n  },\n  openSettings: () =&gt; ipcRenderer.send('open-settings'),\n  notifySettingsUpdated: () =&gt; ipcRenderer.send('settings-updated'),\n};",

Attempting to load defaults from config_default.json');\n        const defaultPathsToCheck = [\n          path.join(__dirname, '../../config_default.json'),\n          path.resolve('config_default.json'),\n          path.resolve('../config_default.json')\n        ];\n\n        let defaultConfigPath = null;\n        for (const p of defaultPathsToCheck) {\n          if (fs.existsSync(p)) {\n            defaultConfigPath = p;\n            break;\n          }\n        }\n\n        if (defaultConfigPath) {\n          console.log(&#96;Loading default config from: ${defaultConfigPath}&#96;);\n          const defaultData = fs.readFileSync(defaultConfigPath, 'utf8');\n          const defaultConfig = JSON.parse(defaultData);\n          \n          // Create config.json with default values in the same directory as config_default.json\n          const configDir = path.dirname(defaultConfigPath);\n          const newConfigPath = path.join(configDir, 'config.json');\n          fs.writeFileSync(newConfigPath, JSON.stringify(defaultConfig, null, 2), 'utf8');\n          console.log(&#96;Created config.json from defaults at: ${newConfigPath}&#96;);\n          \n          return defaultConfig;\n        } else {\n          console.error('Neither config.json nor config_default.json found. ## Changes Made:

1. **Fixed Icon Configuration**:
   - Changed `"icon": "icon.ico"` to `"icon": "tr_logo.ico"` to match the actual file name

2. **Fixed `config_default.json` Packaging**:
   - Moved `config_default.json` from the `files` array to `extraFiles`
   - This places it outside the `app.asar` archive, making it accessible at runtime
   - Files in `extraFiles` are placed in the resources directory alongside the executable

3. **Updated Path Resolution in `preload.js`**:
   - Added checks for production paths including:
     - `process.resourcesPath` (where `extraFiles` are typically placed)
     - Directory alongside the executable (for portable/installed apps)
     - Development paths (for local development)

When you build the package:
- The icon `tr_logo.ico` will be used for the Windows installer and app icon
- `config_default.json` will be included as an extra file and accessible at runtime
- The app will find `config_default.json` in both development and production environments

You can test this by running `npm run package` and verifying that:
1. The installer/executable has the correct icon
2. `config_default.json` exists in the packaged app's resources directory
3. The app can create `config.json` from `config_default.json` on first run
